qa.q: Which was a new public space in modernising Japan?
qa.e: Department stores, parks and trams were new.

qa.q: In which year was the 'Overcoming Modernity' symposium held?
qa.e: It took place in 1943.

qa.q: Nishitani Keiji defined 'modern' as the unification of which three Western strands?
qa.a: Renaissance, Protestant Reformation and the rise of natural science
qa.e: He named these three strands.

qa.q: What did the 'Overcoming Modernity' symposium discuss?
qa.a: How to be modern without being Western
qa.e: It tackled the dilemma of modernisation and Westernisation.

qa.q: The ideas of 'Overcoming Modernity' were used to support:
qa.e: They backed Japan's claimed mission in Asia and war.

qa.q: Which new media spread in modernising Japan?
qa.e: Mass media transformed information and entertainment.

qa.q: Assertion (A): The 'Overcoming Modernity' symposium opposed Japanese nationalism. Reason (R): The 'Overcoming Modernity' symposium was held in Tokyo in 1943.
qa.a: A is false, but R is true
qa.e: A is false, because its ideas fed ultra-nationalism and militarism; R is true.

qa.q: On which two Japanese cities were atomic bombs dropped in 1945?
qa.e: Atomic bombs were dropped on Hiroshima and Nagasaki.

qa.q: Which American general led the occupation of Japan?
qa.e: General MacArthur led the occupation.

qa.q: Article 9 of Japan's post-war constitution:
qa.a: Renounced war as an instrument of national policy
qa.e: It is the 'no war' clause.

qa.q: In which year did Japanese women vote for the first time?
qa.e: Women voted in the 1946 elections.

qa.q: What happened to the zaibatsu under the occupation?
qa.e: The occupation broke up the big business monopolies.

qa.q: Which 1964 event symbolised Japan's post-war recovery?
qa.e: The Olympics and the Shinkansen marked Japan's revival.

qa.q: Minamata disease was caused by:
qa.e: Industrial mercury poisoning caused Minamata disease.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Japan's post-war constitution is often called a 'peace constitution'. Reason (R): Its Article 9 renounced war as an instrument of national policy.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Both true; Article 9 explains the name.

qa.q: What did the British East India Company sell in China to reverse the outflow of silver?
qa.e: Indian-grown opium was sold in China for silver.

qa.q: The First Opium War was fought from:
qa.e: The First Opium War lasted 1839-42.

qa.q: Which territory was ceded to Britain under the Treaty of Nanjing (1842)?
qa.e: Hong Kong was ceded; treaty ports were opened.

qa.q: Who was sent to Canton to stop the opium trade?
qa.e: Lin Zexu confiscated and destroyed opium.

qa.q: The Taiping Rebellion took place in:
qa.e: The Taiping Rebellion lasted 1850-64.

qa.q: The Boxer uprising of 1900 was:
qa.a: An anti-foreign movement crushed by foreign armies
qa.e: The Boxers opposed foreign influence.

qa.q: Why were treaties like Nanjing called 'unequal treaties'?
qa.a: They were forced on China and favoured foreign powers
qa.e: China had to cede territory and open ports on unfavourable terms.

qa.q: Assertion (A): The Qing dynasty grew stronger throughout the nineteenth century. Reason (R): The Treaty of Nanjing ceded Hong Kong to Britain.
qa.a: A is false, but R is true
qa.e: A is false, because the Qing were weakened by wars, unequal treaties and rebellions; R is true.

qa.q: In which year was the Manchu empire overthrown in China?
qa.e: The Qing (Manchu) empire fell in 1911.

qa.q: Who is regarded as the founder of modern China?
qa.e: Sun Yat-sen led the 1911 republic.

qa.q: Which was NOT one of Sun Yat-sen's Three Principles?
qa.e: The three were nationalism, democracy and socialism.

qa.q: Sun Yat-sen's principle of socialism involved:
qa.e: It aimed to regulate capital and equalise land.

qa.q: The May Fourth Movement of 1919 protested against:
qa.a: The post-war peace conference giving Japan control of former German-held territory in China
qa.e: Students protested against the Versailles decision.

qa.q: Who led the Guomindang after Sun Yat-sen's death?
qa.e: Chiang Kai-shek became the Guomindang leader.

qa.q: Why did the Guomindang fail to win peasant support?
qa.a: Its base was urban and it neglected land reform
qa.e: Sun's land programme was never implemented.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Chiang Kai-shek promoted Confucianism. Reason (R): Chiang Kai-shek fought the warlords and tried to eliminate the communists.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Both are true, but R does not explain A: his military campaigns were a separate part of his programme from his promotion of Confucian values.

qa.q: The Chinese Communist Party was founded in:
qa.e: The CCP was founded in 1921, soon after the Russian Revolution.

qa.q: Mao Zedong based the Chinese revolution mainly on:
qa.e: Mao's strategy relied on peasants.

qa.q: The Long March of 1934-35 ended at:
qa.e: The communists marched to Yanan.

qa.q: Japan invaded China in:
qa.e: The Japanese invasion of 1937 changed the civil war's course.

qa.q: After the communist victory in 1949, the Guomindang retreated to:
qa.e: The Guomindang set up its government in Taiwan.

qa.q: The Great Leap Forward (1958) involved:
qa.e: It aimed at rapid industrialisation through communes and backyard steel furnaces.

qa.q: The 'New Democracy' of 1949 was described as:
qa.a: An alliance of all social classes
qa.e: It was presented as an alliance of classes.

qa.q: Assertion (A): The CCP won the civil war in 1949. Reason (R): Mao relied only on urban factory workers for support.
qa.a: A is true, but R is false
qa.e: A is true; R is false, because Mao's strategy was based on the peasantry.

qa.q: Who launched the Cultural Revolution in China?
qa.e: Mao launched it in the mid-1960s.

qa.q: The Red Guards of the Cultural Revolution were mainly:
qa.e: Young people formed the Red Guards.

qa.q: During the Cultural Revolution, what was valued over expertise?
qa.e: Ideological correctness counted more than professional skill.

qa.q: Which was NOT one of Deng Xiaoping's Four Modernisations?
qa.e: The four were science, industry, agriculture and defence; democracy was Wei's 'fifth'.

qa.q: From which year did Deng Xiaoping begin market reforms?
qa.e: Reforms began in 1978.

qa.q: Who wrote about the 'Fifth Modernisation'?
qa.e: Wei Jingsheng argued for democracy as the fifth modernisation.

qa.q: What happened to the 1989 Tiananmen Square protests?
qa.e: The protests calling for democracy were crushed.

qa.q: Assertion (A): China's reforms after 1978 are called a 'socialist market economy'. Reason (R): A market economy was introduced while the Communist Party kept political control.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Both true; this combination explains the label.

qa.q: Taiwan was a Japanese colony from 1895 until:
qa.e: Japanese rule in Taiwan ended in 1945.

qa.q: Who set up a government in Taiwan after 1949?
qa.e: The Guomindang retreated to Taiwan.

qa.q: In which year was martial law lifted in Taiwan?
qa.e: Martial law ended in 1987.

qa.q: Which dynasty ruled Korea before Japanese colonisation?
qa.e: The Joseon dynasty ruled Korea from 1392 to 1910.

qa.q: Japanese colonial rule over Korea lasted from:
qa.e: Korea was a Japanese colony from 1910 to 1945.

qa.q: After 1945, Korea was divided at the:
qa.e: The 38th parallel divided Korea.

qa.q: The Korean War was fought from:
qa.e: It lasted 1950-53 and ended in an armistice.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Taiwan's economy grew rapidly under Guomindang rule. Reason (R): Taiwan had been a Japanese colony from 1895 to 1945.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Both are true, but colonial status does not by itself explain post-1949 growth; land reform and later policies do.

qa.q: Who was South Korea's first president?
qa.e: Syngman Rhee was the first president.

qa.q: The April Revolution of 1960 in South Korea:
qa.e: Student-led protests against rigged elections forced Rhee out.

qa.q: Park Chung-hee came to power in 1961 through:
qa.e: He seized power in a military coup.

qa.q: South Korea's growth strategy under Park was:
qa.e: The state directed export-led industrial growth.

qa.q: Chaebols are:
qa.e: Chaebols like Samsung and Hyundai led industrialisation.

qa.q: The Saemaul Undong was a movement for:
qa.e: The New Village Movement aimed to develop rural areas.

qa.q: The Yushin Constitution of 1972:
qa.e: It allowed Park to remain in office indefinitely.

qa.q: Assertion (A): South Korea's rapid growth came with authoritarian rule. Reason (R): Park Chung-hee came to power by winning a free election in 1961.
qa.a: A is true, but R is false
qa.e: A is true; R is false, because Park seized power in a military coup in 1961.

qa.q: The Gwangju uprising for democracy took place in:
qa.e: The Gwangju uprising of 1980 was brutally suppressed.

qa.q: What did the June Democratic Struggle of 1987 achieve?
qa.e: It forced the introduction of direct presidential elections.

qa.q: South Korea joined the OECD in:
qa.e: South Korea became an OECD member in 1996.

qa.q: During the 1997 Asian financial crisis, South Korean citizens:
qa.a: Donated gold to help the country repay its debts
qa.e: The gold-collecting campaign showed public commitment to recovery.

qa.q: Which statement best summarises Japan's road to modernisation?
qa.a: State-led industrialisation, then imperialism and war, then democracy after 1945
qa.e: That was Japan's sequence.

qa.q: Which statement best summarises China's road to modernisation?
qa.a: Revolution and communism, then market reforms under one-party rule
qa.e: China's path ran through revolution to later market reforms.

qa.q: Under whom was the Gwangju uprising suppressed?
qa.e: Chun Doo-hwan took power after Park and crushed the uprising.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Japan and China followed identical paths to modernisation. Reason (R): China adopted market reforms after 1978.
qa.a: A is false, but R is true
qa.e: A is false, because Japan took a state-led industrial path and China a revolutionary one; R is true.
